A1/I1 + I2 resolved. In src/Uinsure.Policies.Api/Contracts/SellPolicyRequest.cs:63, the shape check is now `amount > MaxAmount || amount % 0.01m != 0`. The `amount * 100` is gone, so nothing in the check can overflow. An amount with at most 2 decimal places and any negative value now reaches the domain and gets the 422 SELL-7 (docs/requirements.md:63). The 400 for more than 2 decimal places or more than 1,000,000.00 is unchanged. 527.180 is still accepted, by value, per David's H6 ruling. No banned rounding API is used (the `%` operator is not on the banned list), and gate.build shows 0 warnings.

A1/I1 + I2 tests. tests/Uinsure.Policies.Api.Tests/SellAmountOverflowTests.cs runs in Production with log capture. For -1e27 and decimal.MinValue it asserts no 500, no Error-level log and nothing stored. In SellAmountShapeTests.cs:104-129, the same two amounts must give the 422 SELL-7 through ProblemAssert.SingleRuleViolation (status, problem+json, type, ruleId, a single entry in violations[]), echo the literal amount and store nothing. gate.finding-red@4ccdcf3 shows these four tests failing with 500 before the fix. gate.green@8b13192 shows them passing after it.

A1/I5 resolved as coverage. Policy.cs was correct and did not change. The 12 two-term tests restore 2026-11-01..2027-10-31 plus 2027-11-01..2028-10-31 and assert literal dates. Here is how they handle the named mutations. (a) LatestTerm => Terms[0] is killed by Latest_term_of_a_two_term_policy_is_the_second_term (Assert.Same Terms[1]), and also by the Status tests on 2027-11-15 and 2028-10-31, which would read Expired. (b) Pending measured from LatestTerm.Start is killed by Status_on_a_day_inside_the_first_of_two_terms_is_Active (2027-06-01 would read Pending). (c) Expired measured from Terms[0].End is killed by the second-term Active rows. (d) CurrentTerm always returning LatestTerm is killed by Current_term_on_a_day_inside_the_first_of_two_terms (expects Terms[0]). (e) A fallback to Terms[0] is killed by Current_term_before_the_first_start_of_two_terms_is_the_latest_term (expects Terms[1]). (f) Making Covers exclusive at either end is killed by the end-day-of-first and start-day-of-second rows. I found no mutation receipt (gate.red-guards) for I5, so this analysis is my own and was not run. The tests are fit for purpose.
